name: The College of Wooster
academic_ranking: Private liberal arts college founded 1866. Ranked #77 among National Liberal Arts Colleges (U.S. News & World Report). Member of the Annapolis Group and listed among 'Colleges That Change Lives.' Known for its signature senior Independent Study (I.S.) research program. Most popular majors: Political Science, Psychology, Biology.
financial_aid: Tuition and fees for 2026-27 are $66,290; total comprehensive cost (with housing and meals) is $82,340 before aid. As a D3 institution, no athletic scholarships are offered. About 99% of admitted students receive some form of financial aid; average aid package for FAFSA filers exceeds $55,000. Merit scholarships include Presidential Scholar (full tuition), College Scholar, and Dean's Scholar ($25,000-$43,000). Need-based Wooster Grants, Pell/FSEOG, federal loans, work-study, and tuition exchange programs also available. Frequently cited as a Best Value College.
facilities_notes: Wooster is a NCAA Division III member (Fighting Scots). Primary athletics facility is the Scot Center, a 123,000-sq-ft, $30 million recreation facility opened in 2012 with four multipurpose courts, a 200-meter indoor track, a fitness center, and batting cages for baseball and softball. The Scot Center's 20,000-sq-ft solar roof is noted as one of the largest of any U.S. college facility. No dedicated softball field details were confirmed from public pages.
program_reputation: Softball competes in NCAA Division III in the North Coast Athletic Conference (NCAC). Team X/Twitter handle is @CoWSoftball.
notes: Data gathered from woosterathletics.com softball coaches page, roster page, and staff directory (checked 2026-07); tuition/aid from wooster.edu; academics/facilities from Wikipedia. No individual staff X/Twitter handles are publicly listed (team account is @CoWSoftball). As a D3 program, athletic scholarships are not offered.
